issue.title: cmake: don't export grpc_cpp_plugin when crosscompiling

labels.name: release notes: no
labels.description: Indicates if PR should not be in release notes

repository.name: grpc
repository.description: C++ based gRPC (C++, Python, Ruby, Objective-C, PHP, C#)

issue.body:
Plugin should not be exported for a cross-compilation environment,
because it has to run on a host/build system. If it's exported then
configure stage fails with an error, that imported target references
non-existing file. Even if the file is found, it can't be used on a host.

Signed-off-by: Vyacheslav Yurkov <uvv.mail@gmail.com>

@drfloob

body:
@xhochy Our of curiosity, why do you use `install` for building packages? I guess it might be for getting built artifacts. Is there an alternative way for getting those?

@UVV-gh Could you explain how installing cross-compiled protoc was a problem for your case?

It seems like @xhochy has a different use case, he actually uses cross-compiled gRPC plugins on the target. Yocto-based generated SDK is used on the _host_ for cross-compilation for the target. SDK consists of two sysroots, one for the target and one for the host, the latter would contain gRPC plugins, which would have to be searched manually and substituted to CMake.

There is a pull request to have a proper compilation split support between gRPC libs and gRPC binaries: 
https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/22498

Because in cross compilation, the libs should be compiled for the target and the binaries for the host.
I add it to my Yocto and I have now a proper SDK and a proper cross compilation.

I try to argue that this PR is legit but it has been refused without good points :(

> @xhochy Our of curiosity, why do you use `install` for building packages? I guess it might be for getting built artifacts. Is there an alternative way for getting those?

I'm a bit confused about this question. For CMake-based workflows `cmake … && make install` is the normal way to build and install artefacts. Can you maybe rephrase this?

@UVV-gh would it work in your case if there was a special flag that disabled the installation of the plugins instead of fully removing it from the CMake setup? I would expect the default output of a cross-compiled run to be equal to the non-cross compiled one. The consumers (on the target) of gRPC should in the end not be able to differentiate them.
@xhochy yes, I'm open to any solution, for example something like `gRPC_BUILD_CROSS_SDK` would work for me
